name: MLB-M1 draft stub
summary: Draft MLB parent cartridge scaffolded from MLB-M0. MLB-M1 has no intentional behavior changes yet; it exists to prove that the scaffold, run, snapshot, check, and compare workflow can create a hot-swappable parent model before real M1 changes are added.
keyImprovements: Scaffolds MLB-M1 from MLB-M0 as a draft parent cartridge without activating it.
Keeps MLB-RP36 as a relief addendum consumed by MLB-M1 instead of treating the reliever shadow artifact as a separate parent model.
Adds a May 30 closeout gate so side predictions must flow into `mlb_side_predictions` and `mlb_side_backtests` before postmortem lessons are trusted.
Adds a cartridge-local performance index and quiet-start full-game gate so May 30 failures can affect the next slate instead of staying as notes.
Persists daily hitter platoon split snapshots so the prop model can be audited against the exact split context shown pregame.
Extracts model-neutral odds, participant, signal, structured-context, and match-factory contracts into models/shared/sports-core while MLB-M1 keeps only MLB adapters and MLB-specific scoring logic.
Moves MLB-M1 workflows and publish lanes into the cartridge while old pipeline paths remain compatibility launchers.
Adds a documented pipeline ownership boundary so data plumbing and offline research are not mistaken for missed model code.
Adds a component registry for sides, first-five, totals, props, HRs, market context, and MLB-RP36 so future work can land in the right model lane without scanning the whole cartridge.
Indexes MLB-M1 and MLB-RP36 run snapshots into shared warehouse model-run tables so performance/backtest queries no longer depend only on JSON files.
Adds registry-aware MLB lifecycle wrappers so future parent models can be scaffolded, run, snapshotted, checked, and compared without hardcoding package scripts to MLB-M1.
Adds an app adapter registry so future active parent models must register their app-facing contract instead of silently rendering through MLB-M1.
Routes legacy pipeline workflow/publish launchers and web prop-calibration access through registry-aware adapters.
Routes MLB-RP36 package scripts and refresh consumption through registry-aware component wrappers.

notes: MLB-M1 should eventually own the final MLB side, first-five, total, prop, and market-context outputs.
Pipeline internals that remain are classified as fetchers, warehouse commands, compatibility launchers, or offline research; production lane behavior should live in the cartridge.
MLB publish/export package commands enter through `models/mlb/run-cartridge.mjs --entry lane:<lane>`; `pipeline/mlb/publish/` is compatibility only.
`models/shared/sports-core` owns reusable sports contracts; `models/mlb/app-model.js` resolves the active MLB app adapter, and `web/src/lib/sports-model.js` re-exports the app composition path.
Do not promote MLB-RP36 into a standalone parent model; it should feed MLB-M1.
Before a new MLB slate, the prior day must have a results journal plus side prediction/backtest rows so lessons are based on warehouse-settled data.
Quiet-start, traffic-without-conversion, and quiet-first-five risks now suppress full-game side promotion unless another market expression is cleaner.
`MLB-M1_log.md` is the working log for warehouse/model changes that still need lane-specific proof.
Run snapshots remain the reproducibility artifact, but every snapshotted MLB-M1/MLB-RP36 run should also be indexed into the shared warehouse model-run tables.
New parent models should start from the model-iteration runbook and registry-aware wrappers, not by editing package scripts to point at a draft cartridge.
New parent models that alter app-facing match output must register in `models/mlb/app-model.js` before activation.
knownLimitations: Compatibility launchers remain under pipeline/mlb, but they are no longer part of the narrowed MLB-M1 source inventory.
MLB-M1 has no separate app adapter yet because it is not active and currently shares the MLB-M0 app-facing contract.
